providers.title: A smooth nonquadratic affine maximal graph in dimension ten (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There is u in C^infinity(R^10), not a polynomial of degree at most two, with positive definite Hessian at every point, solving the affine maximal equation on R^10. Proved in the last lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Jacobi's formula
providers.scope: For invertible M, the derivative of det(M + eps N) at eps = 0 is det(M) tr(M^(-1) N).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cofactors of a Hessian are divergence free
providers.scope: For u of class C^3 with invertible Hessian, the cofactor matrix U = det(D^2u)(D^2u)^(-1) is symmetric with sum_i d_i U^(ij) = 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: First variation of the affine area
providers.scope: For u of class C^4 with positive definite Hessian and compactly supported C^2 variations, the derivative of the affine area is (1/(n+2)) times the integral of phi sum U^(ij) d_ij w; u solves the equation if and only if all these derivatives vanish.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hessian of sqrt(F^2 + t^2)
providers.scope: In a suitable basis the Hessian is block diagonal with blocks (F/u) D^2F and F^2/u^3; det D^2u = F^(m+2) u^(-(m+3)) det D^2F, and D^2u > 0 when D^2F > 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reduction to two equations (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If F, P > 0, D^2F > 0, det D^2F = F P^(-gamma) and tr((D^2F)^(-1) D^2P) + (m+2) P/F = 0, then sqrt(F^2 + t^2) solves the affine maximal equation in m + 1 variables with positive definite Hessian.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The radial system
providers.scope: For radial F, P with y = F' > 0 and y' > 0, the two equations are equivalent to y^(m-1) y' = r^(m-1) F P^(-gamma) and (y^(m-1) P')' = -(m+2) r^(m-1) P^(1-gamma).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The fixed point in s = r^2/2
providers.scope: For small delta the integral equations for (f, p) on [-delta, delta] have a unique solution near (1, 1); it is smooth, with f'(0) = 1 and p'(0) = -(m+2)/m.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A radial solution through the origin (OpenAI)
providers.scope: F = f(|x|^2/2) and P = p(|x|^2/2) are smooth and positive near 0, with D^2F(0) = I, D^2F > 0, and solve the radial system for 0 < r < epsilon with y, y' > 0 and P' < 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Maximal solutions and continuation
providers.scope: Every initial value problem with a C^1 right side has a maximal solution; if its right end is finite, the solution leaves every compact subset of the domain.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The autonomous system (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For m = 9, A = ry/F, B = ry'/y and D = -rP'/(PB) satisfy an autonomous polynomial system in log r and tend to (0, 1, 0) as r tends to 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The invariant box (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The box [0, 9/2] x [0, 7/2] x [0, 33/7] is forward invariant for the autonomous system; its upper corner is a zero of the field.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Existence for all radii (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For m = 9 the radial solution exists for all r > 0 with F, P, F', F'' > 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
